chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from the one whom he mentioned, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, Allah, Exalted is His Remembrance, protects the one who protects His friend.

key_terms.جَلَّ ذِكْرُهُ: Exalted is His Remembrance (a honorific for Allah)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for protecting one's friend according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the concept of divine reciprocity (mu'atabah), where Allah’s preservation of the believer is directly linked to their fidelity toward their close companions. In Shia scholarly tradition, this extends beyond mere social loyalty to include spiritual guardianship, reflecting the broader theme of 'awliya' (friends/allies of God) who protect one another in faith. It serves as a practical reminder that maintaining strong, righteous bonds is a means of securing divine care in this life and the Hereafter.
